de.my_domain.abalone.model

Class Abalone

  • java.lang.Object
    • de.my_domain.abalone.model.Abalone
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    Board, java.lang.Cloneable

    public class Abalone
extends java.lang.Object
implements Board, java.lang.Cloneable
    The Abalone Game implementation. Abalone is a class which implements the family game Abalone using the Interface Board. This class allows a game play against a machine. The class implements the interface Board as well as the mark-up interface Cloneable. It provides all the methods needed to play the game via methods declared in the interface Board.

    • Constructor Detail

      • Abalone

        public Abalone(int size,
               int level,
               Player first)
        The Abalone constructor returns Abalone object and sets its size, difficulty of the machine player as level, and the first player which makes a move. It also initializes the board and the two ball lists which inherit the machine and the human balls.
        Parameters:
        size - Is the size of the returned board.
        level - Is the difficulty of the machine player.
        first - Is the first player allowed to make a move.
        Throws:
        java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - When the size is smaller than 7 or odd and when the level is set to a number smaller than 1 an Exception is thrown.

      • move

        public Board move(int rowFrom,
                  int diagFrom,
                  int rowTo,
                  int diagTo)
        Executes a human move. Eliminating own balls is allowed. This method does not change the state of this instance, which is treated here as immutable. Instead, a new board/game is returned, which is a copy of this with the move executed.
        Specified by:
        move in interface Board
        Parameters:
        rowFrom - The slot's row number from which the ball of the human player should be moved.
        diagFrom - The slot's diagonal number from which the ball of the human player should be moved.
        rowTo - The slot's row number to which the ball of the human player should be moved.
        diagTo - The slot's diagonal number to which the ball of the human player should be moved.
        Returns:
        A new board with the move executed. If the move is not valid, then null will be returned.
        Throws:
        java.lang.IllegalStateException - If the game is already over, or it is not the human's turn.
        java.lang.IllegalArgumentException - If the provided parameters are invalid, e.g., the from slot lies outside the grid or the to slot outside the grid plus an one-element border.

      • toString

        public java.lang.String toString()
        Gets the string representation of this board as row x diagonals hexagon. Each slot is represented by one the three chars '.', 'X', or 'O'. '.' means that the slot currently contains no ball. 'X' means that it contains a black tile. 'O' means that it contains a white tile.

      • evaluateSituation

        private double evaluateSituation(int depth)
        The evaluateSituation method provides an easy way of evaluating the current state of an Abalone object out of the perspective of the computer player. The method is normally used in a tree to decide, which board is more beneficial for the computer than another.
        Parameters:
        depth - The depth is the depth within the tree the board is at. The depth is 0 for the root node.
        Returns:
        A double evaluation of the board is returned. The higher the evaluation the better the board for the computer player.

      • getBestMove

        private Board getBestMove()
        The getBestMove method is called when the machine player needs know the next best possible move it could make. It first generates a tree and uses a min-max-algorithm to evaluate the Abalone boards. It should only be called when it is the machine players turn.
        Returns:
        The most beneficial board for the machine is returned.

      • generateTree

        private static void generateTree(Node parent,
                                 int height)
        The generateTree method is a recursive method, which generates a game tree of a given height and adds it to a Node. The game tree inherits all the possible player moves which can be executed. It is supposed to start with all the machine move first and then, in the next level of the tree executes all possible moves of the next player.
        Parameters:
        parent - Is the parent node to which the resulting children are added to result in a tree. For the initial call of the method it is usually the root Node.
        height - Is the resulting height of the tree. For the initial call of the method it is usually the current game level.

      • updateMinMaxEvaluation

        private static void updateMinMaxEvaluation(Node parent)
        The updateMinMaxEvaluation method is called only once on the completely build tree. It utilizes the min-max-algorithm for updating the evaluation values in the tree. The min-max-algorithm adds the greatest evaluation of its children to a parent node if the next player of the state is the machine, and respectively the smallest if the next player is human, hereby assuming that the human would always make the most hostile move that could possibly be done.
        Parameters:
        parent - Is the node for which an update of the evaluation is to be made. For the initial call of the method it is usually the root node of the tree.
